thread:
maria: FYI opened PR #452 to change the gpu-nodepool TF. TL;DR: make p4d.24xlarge the preferred instance, add spot fallback to p3dn/g4dn, and add optional capacity_reservation support for a single AZ. Need quick review before I merge tomorrow morning. Link: <https://git.company/redwood/infra/pull/452>
jon: quick question — are we sure we want actual Capacity Reservations (CR)? those lock capacity and cost money. For inference-critical lanes sure, but for general nodepool maybe prefer on-demand baseline + spot for scale.
maria: agreed. I added a var.enable_capacity_reservation = false default. Only turned on for the prod-inference workspace. The TF snippet I used in the LT is:

```hcl
resource "aws_launch_template" "gpu_lt" {
  name_prefix   = "gpu-"
  image_id      = data.aws_ami.cuda.id
  instance_type = var.primary_instance_type # p4d.24xlarge

  capacity_reservation_specification {
    capacity_reservation_preference = var.enable_capacity_reservation ? "open" : "none"
    capacity_reservation_target {
      capacity_reservation_id = var.capacity_reservation_id
    }
  }

  user_data = base64encode(templatefile("userdata.sh.tpl", {}))
}
```

maria: note — for mixed instance policy we keep p4d as base and allow p3dn/g4dn for spot fallback via mixedInstancesPolicy on the autoscaling group in another TF module.
lee: heads up: CRs are AZ-scoped and don't mix well with mixedInstancesPolicy (and managed node groups). If we need CRs, we should create a separate dedicated ASG (on-demand) pinned to the CR AZ and keep the mixed spot ASG separate. Otherwise the LT CR block will be ignored for spot/ASG combos in some cases.
jon: good point. Also we should add explicit node labels and taints so workloads land on the right instance type. e.g. add kubelet args:

--node-labels=redwood.dev/gpu=p4d,redwood.dev/role=inference
--register-with-taints=nvidia.com/gpu=present:NoSchedule

maria: done — labels and taints added in userdata and in the nodegroup module. I also set max_unavailable and max_surge for rolling updates to 1 to avoid mass disruption.
jon: for cost control, consider instance weighting and on_demand_base_capacity on the ASG so we keep e.g. 1 on-demand p4d and then spot for scale. Also add lifecycle hooks to drain nodes before termination (spot handling).
maria: added lifecycle hook and node-drainer daemonset. I used a var.spot_fallback_order = ["p4d.24xlarge", "p3dn.24xlarge", "g4dn.12xlarge"] in the module. Any objections to that ordering?
lee: ordering looks fine. One more ask: make sure the capacity_reservation_id is injected via secret manager and not hardcoded in TF vars file. Otherwise it's easy to leak.
maria: yep it's pulled from AWS Secrets Manager via tfdata and only passed in prod pipeline. Example in the pipeline is:

```hcl
variable "capacity_reservation_id" {
  type = string
  default = ""
}

# in CI: TERRAFORM_VAR_capacity_reservation_id = sm://prod/gpu-cr-id
```

jon: pinging @lee for a quick approve after those changes. If no objections by EOD I'll merge and kick off a canary deploy to prod-inference.
deploy-bot: terraform plan for infra/gpu-nodepool (branch: gpu-pr-452) finished: \n  Plan: 3 to add, 0 to change, 0 to destroy. (run id: tf-2026-03-17-11)
maria: :thumbsup: thanks everyone. I'll merge tomorrow morning and watch the canary metrics closely. If we see any pod evictions we fall back to the previous nodegroup config via the rollout policy.
